title: The Doggy Dream Home Tour
clue: Two properties are about to go on the market, and the only buyer has yet to see either.
reveal: Kids stage two cozy spots, write the listings and play real estate agents, while the dog tours both and decides. The deal closes when the dog settles: SOLD, or no offer, and either one is a fair result.
objective: Stage two rest spots, show them to your dog as properties, and let the dog choose or turn both down.
instructions: Kids choose two properties from four options the adult offers: a folded blanket in a quiet corner, a towel in a sunny patch, a cardboard box on its side with a towel in it (tape and staples out), or a blanket draped over two chairs with both ends open.
Stage the two, a few steps apart. Each agent writes a one-line listing (this is the bit that goes wrong in the best way) and draws a quick floor plan of the room with both properties marked.
Everyone sits on the sofa or a rug at the other end of the room. An adult stays with the dog; the Announcer says in a quiet voice, 'Ladies and gentlemen, the buyer is entering the property.'

First viewing: the adult walks toward property A and lets the dog look, sniff, step in, lie down or skip. Never lure, push, or hold the dog in. If the dog goes elsewhere, that is an off-market listing, and kids write it up.
Second viewing: the same at property B. The dog may revisit, ignore both or settle on one.
Close the deal when the dog settles or after ten minutes. The kids stay seated while the adult places a SOLD card, or a NO OFFER card, next to the property from a distance.
Leave the dog in the property it picked. The kids read the final listing and the sale price out loud once (the average price is one sniff and a nap).
twist: The listings are written before the buyer has seen the properties, so the agents are pitching blind and the buyer ignores all of it.
variations: One kid: one agent stages and announces, the adult holds the dog's leash if needed.
Easier: one property only; the dog says yes or no.
Dog-only budget: all properties already in the home (the sofa, the dog bed, the hallway rug); the agents just write the listings.
Seated adult version: the dog is on a long line; the adult sits and lets the dog drift to each spot.
completion: Counts when the dog has seen both properties and either settled in one or left, and the deal card is placed.
photoIdea: The SOLD or NO OFFER card beside the chosen property, with the dog's tail, paw or nose visible at the edge of the frame.
memoryPrompt: Which listing did the dog buy, or what did the dog buy that nobody listed?
supplies: Paper, pens and a few cards
safety: Kids stay seated away from the dog; a dog in a spot is off limits, and nobody calls, crowds or blocks the exit.
Dens are open at both ends, never closed in, no tape or staples; take the box away if it gets chewed.
Use dog spots only: do not place the dog in a child's bed or a spot where it might be startled.
